standard: GDD rework v2 · 80+ researched scenarios · scorecard-passed
note: Diverse routes to family: adoption/fostering, surrogacy & IVF/ART, single & LGBTQ+ parenthood, blended and childfree, and the gendered & legal barriers (UNESCO 8.1, 1.1, 2.2). New v2 build, the equity node closing Chapter 7 and the counterpart to If, When & Whether (g59), for everyone whose route to parenthood isn't the default biological one. Six modes: every route is real family (bust 'real family is only biological'; adoptive, single, queer, blended and childfree families are fully real), the routes (what adoption, fostering, IVF/ART, surrogacy, single and LGBTQ+ parenthood each involve, with the right official first step), the real path (honest steps, timelines, costs and emotions; no romanticising and no false hope; setbacks aren't a verdict), name the barriers (India's specific, gendered and legal barriers, told honestly so people aren't blindsided: under CARA 2022 a single man may adopt a boy but not a girl while a single woman may adopt any gender; the Surrogacy and ART Acts 2021 are altruistic-only and mainly for married couples; and since Supriyo v. Union of India (Oct 2023) same-sex marriage is not legally recognised, so same-sex couples cannot marry or jointly adopt, though a single LGBTQ+ person can adopt as a single applicant), your family your way (dignity, chosen family, support, family acceptance on your terms), tools & help (the routes/eligibility reference, CARA and licensed clinics, current dated legal info). Every family form treated with full dignity, none framed as lesser; LGBTQ+ content handled with the care of Spectrum (no outing); legal/eligibility content is general, dated and evolving, not legal advice, and is to be verified and localised. Builds on Spectrum (g32) and Your Path, Your Call (g54). India: real, specific barriers (CARA single-man girl-child rule, surrogacy/ART restrictions, no same-sex marriage or joint adoption, single-mother stigma), with official routes via CARA and licensed ART clinics.

evidenceBase: Family is built in many valid ways and a non-biological or non-default family is fully real: adoptive, single-parent, LGBTQ+, blended and childfree families are all real, and what children need most is stable, loving care rather than a particular family shape, so 'real family is only biological', 'adopted children are less your own' and 'a single parent isn't enough' are myths to retire. Every route, adoption, fostering, IVF/ART, surrogacy, solo and queer parenthood, deserves dignity and no route or family form is lesser (UNESCO ITGSE Key Concept 1 families & 2 values and inclusion; child-wellbeing research on stability and care over family structure)

Each route is a real journey with honest steps, costs, waits and emotions rather than an instant or guaranteed result, and the node is honest about India's specific, partly gendered and legal barriers so people go in informed rather than blindsided: under the CARA Adoption Regulations 2022 a single man may adopt a boy but not a girl while a single woman may adopt a child of any gender and a married couple in a stable two-year marriage may adopt any gender; the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act 2021 permits only altruistic surrogacy and mainly for married couples, and the ART (Regulation) Act 2021 is for infertile married couples and women. Naming a barrier is going in informed, not endorsing it as fair, and difficulty or a setback on a route is not a verdict that family 'wasn't meant to be' (CARA Adoption Regulations 2022; Surrogacy and ART Regulation Acts 2021)

Barriers are real and so are the open doors, and the law is specific and evolving: in Supriyo v. Union of India (17 October 2023) the Supreme Court declined to legally recognise same-sex marriage, leaving it to Parliament, so same-sex couples cannot currently marry or jointly adopt in India, yet a single LGBTQ+ person can still adopt as a single applicant and chosen family is real and often a great strength. Every family form is treated with full dignity and none as lesser, LGBTQ+ content is handled with care and without outing, and the legal and eligibility material is general, dated and to be verified with official, current sources (CARA, licensed clinics or a legal expert) rather than rumour, and is not legal advice (Supriyo v. Union of India 2023; CARA; India ART/surrogacy law, current as of 2024-25 and evolving)

options.text: Stay open to the route that actually fits your life
options.consequence: You choose on fit, not snobbery.

options.text: Cling to one 'respectable' route out of prejudice
options.consequence: Staying open finds the route that fits; route-snobbery narrows your options for no good reason.

scenarios.debrief: Choose the route that fits your life, not the one prejudice calls the only respectable one.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a permanent route to parenthood, or a temporary or supportive arrangement?
scenarios.relearn: Adoption and surrogacy lead to permanent parenthood; short-term fostering and respite care are temporary.

items.text: Respite care for a few weeks

scenarios.hook: Spot the accurate way to think about choosing a route.
scenarios.relearn: Choose a route by fit and real understanding, not by price or assumption.

scene.text: Match the route to your life and circumstances
Assume the priciest route is the best
Learn each route's real process first

scenarios.why: Matching to your life and learning the process is accurate; assuming priciest-is-best isn't.

scenarios.hook: Your partner is discouraged after a setback in the process. You want to steady them.
scenarios.relearn: Naming a setback as a step, not the end, and reaching for support keeps you both moving as a team.

yourLine.text: "This is a hard step, not the end, let's breathe, get support, and decide the next move together."
"Maybe it's a sign we should just stop."

scenarios.hook: Someone tells you to 'just relax and it'll happen' as you navigate a hard route. You want to set them straight kindly.
scenarios.relearn: Kindly correcting 'just relax' and naming what helps protects you from a dismissive myth.

yourLine.text: "It's more complex than relaxing, but thank you, what helps is steady support."
"Yeah, maybe I'm overthinking it."

scenarios.hook: The emotional weight of the journey is building and you're carrying it alone.
scenarios.relearn: Get support, partner, community or counselling, before the journey overwhelms you.

options.text: Reach for support, partner, community or counselling, before you're overwhelmed
options.consequence: You carry the journey with help, not alone.

options.text: Bottle it up and push through solo
options.consequence: Reaching for support carries the weight together; bottling it up risks burnout on an already hard path.

scenarios.debrief: Reach for support on a hard family-building journey before overwhelm; you needn't carry it alone.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a healthy expectation of the journey, or a setup for disappointment?
scenarios.relearn: Expecting waits, setbacks and needing support is healthy; 'first try or never' and 'zero doubt' set you up to hurt.

items.text: There may be waits and setbacks
It must work first try or never
Real parents feel zero doubt ever

scenarios.hook: Match each feeling on the journey to a kind, true response.
scenarios.relearn: Discouragement, overwhelm and doubt each have a kind, true response that keeps you going.

pairs.right: It's a step, not a verdict

pairs.left: Overwhelm at the cost or wait
pairs.right: Get support and reassess calmly
Devoted, supported care is enough

scenarios.hook: A young queer relative says they've been told they can 'never' have a family in India. You want honesty plus hope.
scenarios.relearn: Honest-with-hope names the real bar and the open door, instead of a crushing, untrue blanket 'never'.

yourLine.text: "Couples can't marry or adopt jointly yet, but you can adopt as a single, and chosen family is real, let's get the facts."
"Yeah, sadly that's just true, no family for you."

scenarios.hook: You're tempted to use an unlicensed shortcut someone offered to dodge the legal barriers.
scenarios.relearn: Choose lawful official routes over a risky shortcut, even when the barriers are frustrating.

options.text: Stay with lawful, official routes even though they're harder
options.consequence: You protect yourself and any child involved.

options.text: Take the risky shortcut to skip the hurdles
options.consequence: Lawful routes protect you and the child; an unlicensed shortcut risks fraud, harm and a child's safety.

scenarios.debrief: Stick to lawful, official routes despite the barriers; unlicensed shortcuts risk you and the child.

scenarios.hook: Sort: accurate about who can use surrogacy in India now, or a misconception?
scenarios.relearn: Altruistic-only and mainly-married-couples are accurate for surrogacy now; free commercial and easy single-man access are not.

items.text: Any single man can easily access it

scenarios.hook: Sam: knowing the barriers and the open doors lets you fight smart and protect your hope. Useful?
scenarios.relearn: Knowing the barriers and the open doors lets you act smart and keep hope.
scenarios.affirm: Knowing both the barriers and the open doors lets you act strategically and protect your hope.

scenarios.hook: At a gathering, someone interrogates your single-parent choice. You want a calm, closing line.
scenarios.relearn: A calm 'chosen with care, loved and thriving, at peace' affirms your family and ends the interrogation.

yourLine.text: "I chose this with care, my child is loved and thriving, and I'm at peace with it."
"I know, I know, it's not ideal..."

scenarios.hook: Your child asks why your family looks different from their friends'. You want to answer with warmth.
scenarios.relearn: Telling a child families come in many shapes, bound by love, gives them pride and a true frame.

yourLine.text: "Families come in many shapes, and ours is built on love, that's what makes it a family."
"Don't worry about what others think."

scenarios.hook: You're letting relatives' disapproval keep you from celebrating your family openly.
scenarios.relearn: Live your family openly and with pride; their disapproval doesn't get to keep it hidden.

options.text: Choose to live and celebrate your family with quiet pride
options.consequence: Your joy stops shrinking to fit their doubt.

options.text: Keep your family low-key to avoid their reactions
options.consequence: Living with quiet pride reclaims your joy; staying low-key to avoid reactions lets their doubt rule your home.

scenarios.debrief: Live and celebrate your family with quiet pride; don't shrink it to fit relatives' disapproval.

scenarios.hook: Sort: builds a thriving non-default family, or undermines it?
scenarios.relearn: Support and confidence build a thriving family; constant apology and hiding undermine it.

items.text: Hiding your family from the world

scenarios.hook: Spot what helps a child in a non-default family thrive.
scenarios.relearn: Children in non-default families thrive on loving care and pride, not taught shame.

scene.text: Loving, stable, present care
Being taught to feel ashamed of their family
Pride and honesty about who they are

scenarios.why: Loving stable care and pride help a child thrive; teaching shame about their family harms them.

scenarios.hook: A colleague spreads a confident but wrong 'fact' about adoption eligibility. You want to correct gently.
scenarios.relearn: Gently pointing to the official CARA source corrects misinformation without a confrontation.

yourLine.text: "Actually the current CARA rules differ, it's worth checking the official source before deciding."
"Hmm, you're probably right."

scenarios.hook: "Once you know the rules today, you never need to check again."
scenarios.relearn: Family-building rules can change; verify the current law when you act, don't rely on old knowledge.

myth.un: Once you know the rules today, you never need to check again.
myth.re: Family-building law and eligibility can change, so verifying the current rules when you act is part of doing it right.
myth.why: Current beats remembered when law evolves.

scenarios.hook: Spot the trustworthy move when starting a route to family.
scenarios.relearn: Start with official bodies and current law; an offer to skip the law is a red flag.

scene.text: Going to CARA or a licensed clinic
Trusting an agent who promises to skip the law
Checking current, dated legal information

scenarios.why: CARA, licensed clinics and current legal info are trustworthy; an agent promising to skip the law is a red flag.
